narrativeReportMd:
# Task R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps the same `Task` resource identity, but the local content model has multiple hard R4-to-R6 breaks and several high-risk R6-to-R4 gaps. The largest migration concerns are the `focus` wrapper remodel, removal/merge of `instantiates*`, `performerType`, and `reason*` fields, the new `restriction` invariant, and the R6-only `doNotPerform` modifier.

## Scope
This report covers Task-owned elements, constraints, bindings, flags, and reference/type domains from the local R4 and R6 core packages. Inherited Resource/DomainResource/base datatype changes are excluded and noted as dependencies.

## Main migration themes
Task R6 consolidates several paired or direct elements into richer wrappers: direct references become `BackboneElement.value[x]`, code/reference pairs become `CodeableReference`, and requested/actual performers are separated. These changes improve expressivity but require structural transforms. R6 also tightens fulfillment semantics through `tsk-1` and introduces a modifier for negated tasks.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are `Task:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:Task.instantiates:8b2f1a`, `Task:TYPE_DOMAIN:Task.focus:1c4d72`, `Task:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:Task.performerType-requestedPerformer:f47b9c`, `Task:REFERENCE_TARGET:Task.owner-performer:6db342`, `Task:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:Task.reason:0a73e8`, `Task:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:Task.restriction:aa0e61`, and `Task:FLAGS_AND_MODIFIERS:Task.doNotPerform:df5019`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important where migration depends on workflow meaning: external `instantiatesUri`, owner vs performer semantics, reasonCode plus reasonReference pairing, restriction semantics, and `doNotPerform` downgrade safety.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many breaks could have been softened by deprecated aliases or parallel fields, but R6 appears to favor unified modeling around `focus`, `CodeableReference`, and explicit modifier semantics. The tradeoff is cleaner R6 semantics at the cost of non-trivial transforms for R4 payloads.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should cover CodeableReference and datatype-level changes, DomainResource inherited constraints, Task search parameters, and full terminology expansions.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Task has substantial local R4->R6 breaking changes despite stable resource identity. Top concerns are structural remodels of `focus`/`reason`/performer fields, removed formal-definition fields, and the safety-critical R6-only `doNotPerform` modifier. The main uncertainty is official migration intent for `instantiatesUri` and other semantic transforms.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mostly not about cardinality minimum increases; it is about representation changes. R4 direct elements often become R6 wrappers (`focus.value[x]`, CodeableReference), several old fields are renamed or merged, reference target domains change, and R6 introduces new semantics for negated tasks and restriction validity. R6-to-R4 conversion needs explicit loss policies for multiple foci/reasons, CodeableReference references, new datatypes, and modifier content.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, flag, and binding changes because both StructureDefinitions and local terminology files were parsed directly. Confidence is medium for justification, prevalence, and detailed terminology effects because official diffs, live expansions, and production instances were not available.

findings.title: Task.instantiatesCanonical and Task.instantiatesUri were removed

oldState.summary: R4 had two optional formal-definition elements: instantiatesCanonical and instantiatesUri.
oldState.narrativeMd: `Task.instantiatesCanonical` could point at a FHIR ActivityDefinition; `Task.instantiatesUri` could carry an externally maintained protocol/workflow URI.

newState.summary: R6 has no Task.instantiatesCanonical or Task.instantiatesUri elements.
newState.narrativeMd: The closest native R6 pattern appears to be using `Task.focus.valueCanonical` with an appropriate `Task.code` such as `instantiate`, but R6 has no `focus.valueUri` choice for arbitrary external URIs.

facts.note: R6 focus.value[x] allows Reference or canonical, not uri.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 Task StructureDefinition contains no same-named elements. The new `focus.valueCanonical` plus `Task.code` pattern is a plausible migration target for FHIR canonical definitions, not a formally declared rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct structural validation break: an R4 Task containing either removed element has an unknown element under the R6 Task definition. The canonical case may often be transformable, but arbitrary external `instantiatesUri` content has no native R6 URI slot and may require an extension or out-of-band mapping.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Workflow automation can lose the formal definition that tells a recipient how to execute the task, especially for external workflow languages carried in `instantiatesUri`.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal of making `focus` the focal target for task action is reasonable, and the canonical case fits that remodel. A less-breaking design was available, but it would preserve duplicate same-resource ways to identify a formal definition and would keep the arbitrary URI case outside the unified `focus.value[x]` model. With those material modeling tradeoffs and no official rationale in the inputs, the break is best assessed as probably justified rather than clearly unavoidable.
justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate task action targets in `focus` and represent instantiation as task semantics rather than separate instantiates fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated instantiatesCanonical/instantiatesUri while adding the R6 focus-based canonical pattern.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `Task.instantiatesCanonical` and `Task.instantiatesUri` as deprecated aliases for at least one release, while introducing `focus.valueCanonical` plus task-code guidance for new R6 content. This would preserve all R4 instances, including external workflow URIs, but would require precedence and consistency rules when both old instantiates fields and new focus-based representation are populated.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 payloads, especially external URIs, but leaves overlapping formal-definition locations and weakens the focus consolidation.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Task.instantiatesCanonical` as 0..1 canonical targeting ActivityDefinition.
R4 defines `Task.instantiatesUri` as 0..1 uri for externally maintained definitions.
No R6 Task element with this id is present.
R6 focus value choices are Reference(Resource) and canonical(CanonicalResource), not uri.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative and includes only the minimum required R4 Task context plus the removed fields.

findings.narrativeMd: `Task.instantiatesCanonical` and `Task.instantiatesUri` disappeared from the R6 Task model. R4 systems that used these fields to bind a Task to a protocol, ActivityDefinition, BPMN process, or other workflow definition will produce payloads that strict R6 validators reject. The FHIR-canonical case has an apparent R6 home in `focus.valueCanonical`, but external URI-only definitions do not.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances containing either element are new-invalid because R6 Task does not define those element names. This primarily affects R4-to-R6 validation, generated serializers, XML schema order, and workflow engines that expected the formal definition in a fixed field. It is not an R6-to-R4 problem for new R6 fields, but migration can be lossy for external URI definitions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory Tasks using either instantiates field. For canonical FHIR definitions, consider mapping to `focus[0].valueCanonical` and setting `Task.code` to an action code such as `instantiate` when semantically correct. For external URIs, use a documented extension, a local profile rule, or an input parameter; do not silently drop the URI. Test both canonical and non-canonical examples.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been made less disruptive by retaining deprecated aliases or adding `focus.valueUri`. The tradeoff is that R6 would preserve duplicate modeling paths for formal definitions, while the chosen design makes `focus` the focal target for task action.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The canonical migration path is inferred from the R6 shape and task-code additions; an official diff or narrative migration note would improve confidence.

findings.title: Task.focus changed from a single Reference to repeating BackboneElement.value[x]

oldState.summary: R4 focus was an optional single Reference(Resource).

semanticText.definition: The request being actioned or the resource being manipulated by this task.
semanticText.comment: If multiple resources need to be manipulated, use sub-tasks.

oldState.narrativeMd: A focused R4 Task encoded the reference directly as `focus: { "reference": "..." }`.

newState.summary: R6 focus is a repeating BackboneElement with required value[x], either Reference(Resource) or canonical(CanonicalResource).

semanticText.definition: The request being fulfilled or the resource being manipulated (changed, suspended, etc.) by this task.
semanticText.comment: Typically a Task should only have one focus; if multiple focuses are provided, action is taken on the set as a whole.

newState.narrativeMd: A focused R6 Task uses a repeating `focus` array whose item has `valueReference` or `valueCanonical`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The path name remains `Task.focus`, but the R6 element is a wrapper around a required choice value rather than the reference itself.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with a direct `focus` reference is structurally invalid in R6 until wrapped as `focus[0].valueReference`. Conversely, R6 can carry multiple foci and canonical foci that cannot be represented in the single R4 Reference field.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Task routing and fulfillment logic commonly depends on the focal request or resource; losing or mis-wrapping focus can change what work is performed.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: R6's goal of supporting canonical foci and tightly coupled multi-focus tasks is reasonable, but replacing a central direct Reference with a BackboneElement wrapper is highly disruptive. A less-breaking design could cover the common R4 Reference case, yet it would not provide the same single, normalized representation for reference, canonical, and repeated foci. Those lasting representation and validation tradeoffs make the chosen break probably justified, not clearly avoidable.
justification.inferredGoal: Allow focus to be either an instance reference or a canonical definition and allow tightly coupled multi-focus tasks.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep direct `Task.focus` Reference and add separate optional fields for canonical or additional foci.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `Task.focus` as `0..1 Reference(Resource)` and add `focusCanonical` and/or an additional-focus backbone for the new cases. Existing R4 instances would remain valid. The cost is that consumers would need to inspect multiple focal-target locations, and deprecated direct focus plus newer canonical/repeated focus mechanisms might accumulate indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve common R4 focus references but split focal-target semantics across multiple fields.

evidence.detail: R4 `Task.focus` is 0..1 Reference(Resource).
R6 `Task.focus` is 0..* BackboneElement.
R6 adds required `value[x]` with Reference(Resource) or canonical(CanonicalResource).

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example uses the old direct-reference representation. The migration example shows the equivalent R6 wrapper form. The R6 canonical example has no native R4 Task.focus representation.

findings.narrativeMd: `Task.focus` is one of the most important Task navigation fields, and R6 changes both its JSON shape and its semantic domain. Existing R4 code that reads `task.focus.reference` must now iterate `task.focus[]` and inspect `valueReference` or `valueCanonical`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `focus` are old-valid/new-invalid until transformed. R6 instances with multiple foci or a canonical focus are not cleanly R4-representable. The change affects strict validators, generated classes, FHIRPath expressions, search implementations, XML element ordering, and business rules that assumed one direct reference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map an R4 direct focus reference to a single R6 `focus` repetition with `valueReference`. For R6-to-R4 downgrade, reject or extension-map canonical foci and decide how to handle multiple foci; flattening to the first value is unsafe unless a profile guarantees equivalence. Regression tests should cover no focus, one reference focus, multiple R6 foci, and canonical focus.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new `focusCanonical` or `definition` element would have been less disruptive, but would split focal-target semantics. The R6 wrapper is coherent but requires every focused R4 Task to be transformed.

findings.title: Task.statusReason changed from CodeableConcept to repeating CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 statusReason was 0..1 CodeableConcept with an example binding and no value set URL.

binding.description: Codes to identify the reason for current status. These will typically be specific to a particular workflow.

oldState.narrativeMd: The reason coding/text appeared directly under `Task.statusReason`.

newState.summary: R6 statusReason is 0..* CodeableReference(Resource) with an example binding to task-status-reason.

binding.description: Codes to identify the reason for current status. These will typically be specific to a particular workflow.

newState.narrativeMd: Codeable content must be nested under `concept`, and R6 may also reference a resource as the status reason.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element name and definition remain aligned, but its type and repeated wire shape changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 `statusReason` object with `coding` or `text` directly under the element is not a valid R6 CodeableReference. R6 reference-only reasons and multiple reasons have no direct R4 statusReason representation.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing status reasons to point to resources is a reasonable R6 goal. The less-breaking alternative is real, but it only partially matches the CodeableReference model because separate coded and reference fields create conflict and pairing questions, especially when multiple reasons are present. Given those material tradeoffs, the same-name CodeableReference break is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer status-reason evidence while preserving coded concepts through CodeableReference.concept.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `statusReason` as CodeableConcept and add a separate reference-capable status reason element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `Task.statusReason` as a repeatable CodeableConcept and added `statusReasonReference` or a similar optional reference field. That would preserve R4 coded/text reasons and cover many reference use cases, but it would reintroduce the code/reference split that CodeableReference is designed to avoid and would need rules for whether a concept and reference describe the same reason or separate reasons.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves coded R4 reasons but keeps a paired code/reference pattern with possible association ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 statusReason is 0..1 CodeableConcept.
R6 statusReason is 0..* CodeableReference(Resource).
R6 supplies an example value set for status reasons.

examples.examplesMd: The old coded reason must be wrapped under `concept` in R6. A reference-only R6 status reason cannot be represented in the R4 statusReason field.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same element name but changes its representation. This is easy to miss because the business meaning is similar; the breaking part is that old `CodeableConcept` children are now nested in `CodeableReference.concept` and the element repeats.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Tasks with `statusReason` can fail R6 validation due to both the type wrapper and array shape. R6 Tasks with multiple reasons or a resource reference reason cannot be faithfully downgraded into R4 `Task.statusReason`, which was a single CodeableConcept.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 `statusReason` as `statusReason[0].concept`. For downgrade, only map a single R6 `concept`; reference-only or multiple reasons require an extension, profile-specific rule, or manual review. Update codegen and FHIRPath expressions that access `statusReason.coding` directly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A parallel `statusReasonReference` would have preserved R4 coded content and avoided a same-name type replacement. R6 instead chooses the common CodeableReference pattern, which is cleaner but not wire-compatible.

findings.title: Task.performerType was replaced by requestedPerformer CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 performerType was 0..* CodeableConcept with preferred performer-role binding.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented the requested performer as one or more role/kind concepts.

newState.summary: R6 requestedPerformer is 0..* CodeableReference with the same preferred performer-role binding on the concept side and target profiles for specific actors.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express either a requested performer role/kind or a specific requested actor reference.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The definitions, requirements, binding name, and binding value set indicate a functional successor, but the R6 element is more expressive and not a pure wire-compatible rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 payloads with `performerType` use an element name that R6 no longer defines. R6 `requestedPerformer.reference` values have no R4 performerType representation because R4 only had a CodeableConcept.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of identifying either the requested performer kind or a specific requested actor is reasonable. However, removing `performerType` and replacing it with a differently named CodeableReference was not clearly necessary to meet that goal. Keeping the R4 role field and adding a reference-oriented requested-performer element would preserve R4 instances while supporting the new actor assignment use case with moderate, manageable tradeoff.
justification.inferredGoal: Broaden requested performer from role kind to role-or-specific-actor using CodeableReference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `performerType` for role/kind concepts and add a separate requested-performer reference field.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backwards-compatible base design could keep `Task.performerType` as the requested role/kind concept, clarify its definition, and add an optional `requestedPerformer` reference or `requestedPerformerReference` for specific actors. This avoids a same-fact duplicate concept path if the new field is reference-only. The tradeoff is less datatype uniformity than CodeableReference and more logic for clients that want a single requested-performer abstraction.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps R4 role content valid with only moderate model complexity from separate role and actor slots.

evidence.detail: R4 defines performerType as 0..* CodeableConcept.
R6 has no performerType element.
R6 defines requestedPerformer as 0..* CodeableReference with actor target profiles.

examples.examplesMd: Role-only R4 content maps cleanly to `requestedPerformer.concept`. R6 reference content is not representable in R4 without an extension or a lossy role derivation.

findings.narrativeMd: This is both a rename and a type expansion. Implementers cannot simply keep emitting `performerType`; R6 expects `requestedPerformer`, and concept values must be inside CodeableReference when using the concept side.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Tasks with `performerType` are new-invalid in R6 until renamed and wrapped. R6 Tasks that name a specific requested performer reference cannot be represented in R4 `performerType`, except by extension or by deriving a less-specific role concept.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `performerType` CodeableConcept to `requestedPerformer[].concept`. For R6-to-R4, only downgrade concept values automatically. Reference values need manual policy: preserve as extension, map to a role, or reject downgrade. Update queueing/routing code and search parameter assumptions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias would have been less disruptive, but the richer CodeableReference design more accurately captures assignment to either a class or a specific participant.

findings.title: Task.owner targets narrowed and actual performers moved to new Task.performer

oldState.summary: R4 owner was the individual, organization, or Device currently responsible for task execution and allowed Device and HealthcareService targets.

semanticText.definition: Individual organization or Device currently responsible for task execution.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 owner could directly be a Device or HealthcareService responsible for execution.

newState.summary: R6 owner is the party responsible for managing execution, drops Device and HealthcareService targets, adds Group, and adds Task.performer.actor for actual performers.

semanticText.definition: Party responsible for managing task execution.

newState.narrativeMd: `Task.performer` is now available for entities who actually performed the task; each performer repetition requires `actor`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The owner element remains but its allowed targets and definition changed; R6 adds a separate performer backbone for actual performers.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances whose `owner` is a Device or HealthcareService can become invalid in R6. R6 instances that use `owner` as Group or record actual actors in `performer` do not downgrade cleanly to R4.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating managerial ownership from actual performance is a reasonable R6 goal, but narrowing `owner` targets was not clearly required to accomplish it. R6 could have added the new `performer` backbone and clarified that owner means management responsibility while still accepting the R4 Device and HealthcareService owner references. That alternative preserves old instances and leaves only moderate long-term ambiguity to manage through definitions, deprecation notes, and profiles.
justification.inferredGoal: Clarify owner as managing party and represent actual performers explicitly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `Task.performer` while retaining Device and HealthcareService as allowed owner targets with clarified owner semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would keep the full R4 `owner` target list, add `Task.performer.actor` for actual performers, and use narrative or profile guidance to discourage using `owner` for execution actors. The tradeoff is that some implementations might continue old ambiguous owner usage, but validators would not reject historical Device or HealthcareService owners solely because of the R6 target list.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 owner references with moderate risk that old owner-as-performer usage persists.

evidence.detail: R4 owner targets include Device and HealthcareService.
R6 owner targets omit Device and HealthcareService and add Group.
evidence.quote: Group included; Device and HealthcareService absent

evidence.detail: R6 adds performer.actor for who performed the task.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 owner Device example is valid under the R4 target list but invalid under the R6 owner target list. The migration target depends on whether the device managed the task or actually performed it.

findings.narrativeMd: `Task.owner` did not merely gain or lose reference targets; its definition moved toward management of execution, while R6 introduces `Task.performer` for actual actors. That means a mechanical target-list migration may be clinically or operationally wrong.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 owner references to Device or HealthcareService are potential old-valid/new-invalid cases. R6 owner Group and any `performer` data are R6-to-R4 representability risks. Runtime code that treated owner as the performer must be reviewed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify each R4 owner value: if it was the managing party and still uses an allowed target, keep it as owner; if it was the actor that performed work, migrate to `performer.actor`; if it is HealthcareService, define a local mapping to Organization/CareTeam, requestedPerformer, performer extension, or reject. Test Device, HealthcareService, Group, and ordinary practitioner/organization cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping R4 targets while adding `performer` would have avoided validation breaks but preserved ambiguous owner semantics. R6 chooses a cleaner separation with target narrowing.

findings.title: Task.reasonCode and Task.reasonReference were merged into repeating Task.reason CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 had separate optional reasonCode CodeableConcept and reasonReference Reference(Resource).

binding.description: Indicates why the task is needed.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could carry at most one coded/text reason and at most one referenced reason in distinct fields.

newState.summary: R6 has one repeating reason element of type CodeableReference(Resource) with an example task-reason value set.
newState.narrativeMd: Each R6 reason repetition can carry either `concept` or `reference`, and multiple reasons are allowed.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same reason semantics are consolidated under a new element name and CodeableReference representation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` contain element names R6 no longer defines. R6 can carry more than one reason or multiple references/concepts, which R4 cannot represent without loss.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Unifying coded and referenced reasons and allowing multiple reasons is a coherent R6 goal. A less-breaking alias strategy would preserve R4 instances, but it would leave old paired fields and new CodeableReference repetitions competing to represent the same rationale. Because that duplication can create validation, search, and interpretation ambiguity, the breaking consolidation is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Unify coded and referenced reasons and allow multiple reasons.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` aliases while adding the R6 repeating `reason` CodeableReference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated fields while adding `reason`. That would let R4 payloads validate unchanged and encourage migration over time. The cost is durable duplication: profiles and clients would need to decide whether old and new fields may both appear, how to merge them, and which representation wins when they conflict.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 reason fields but creates duplicate same-resource reason representations and precedence rules.

evidence.detail: R4 defines reasonCode as 0..1 CodeableConcept.
R4 defines reasonReference as 0..1 Reference(Resource).
R6 defines reason as 0..* CodeableReference(Resource).

examples.examplesMd: If both R4 reason fields are present, migration can produce two R6 reason repetitions, but the original relationship between the concept and reference may be ambiguous.

findings.narrativeMd: The reason fields moved from two R4 siblings to a single repeating R6 CodeableReference. This is a common-looking model cleanup, but strict clients and validators will see it as removed elements plus a new element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Tasks with either old reason field are new-invalid in R6. R6 Tasks with more than one concept, more than one reference, or mixed repeated reasons cannot be downgraded faithfully into R4, which had only one slot for each representation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `reasonCode` to `reason[].concept` and `reasonReference` to `reason[].reference`. If both are present, preserve both and flag for review if local semantics implied that the reference justified the code rather than being an independent reason. For downgrade, allow only profiles that restrict R6 to at most one concept and one reference.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping deprecated aliases would have protected R4 payloads but perpetuated paired reason fields. CodeableReference is coherent and less duplicative, but not wire-compatible.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 example value set is example strength; the break is structural, not a required terminology rejection.

findings.title: Task.restriction gained a local invariant requiring fulfill code and Reference focus

oldState.summary: R4 had the lastModified/authoredOn invariant but no computable restriction/focus/fulfill invariant.

constraints.expression: lastModified.exists().not() or authoredOn.exists().not() or lastModified >= authoredOn

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 narrative described restriction as for fulfillment tasks, but the Task StructureDefinition did not enforce that with a root invariant.

newState.summary: R6 adds error invariant tsk-1: restriction is allowed only for fulfillment tasks with a Reference focus.

constraints.human: Last modified date must be greater than or equal to authored-on date.
constraints.expression: lastModified.exists().not() or authoredOn.exists().not() or lastModified >= authoredOn

constraints.human: Task.restriction is only allowed if the Task is seeking fulfillment and a focus is specified.
constraints.expression: restriction.exists() implies (code.coding.where(code='fulfill' and system='http://hl7.org/fhir/CodeSystem/task-code').exists() and focus.exists() and focus.value.ofType(Reference).exists())

newState.narrativeMd: `tsk-0` preserves the old lastModified/authoredOn rule with a new key; `tsk-1` is the material new restriction rule.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation tightening. R4 Tasks could contain `restriction` without a computable requirement that `code` be `fulfill` and focus be a Reference. Such instances become invalid in R6. Even an R6 canonical-only focus is insufficient when restriction is present.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable because `restriction` is only consistently interpretable when the task fulfills a referenced request. A warning-first rule would be less breaking, but it would only partially meet that goal because semantically unsafe restriction usage would remain base-conformant. Without official rationale the change is not proven absolutely necessary, but the error invariant is probably justified by the interoperability value of enforcing the precondition.
justification.inferredGoal: Prevent use of restriction outside fulfillment of a referenced request.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Introduce the restriction rule first as a warning or best-practice invariant instead of an error.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could add `tsk-1` as a warning, best-practice invariant, or profile-level rule for one release. That would flag questionable R4-style data without rejecting it. The tradeoff is material: receiving systems could still treat `restriction` as valid even when there is no `fulfill` task code or Reference focus to define what request is being restricted.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve loose R4 usage but would not enforce the fulfillment/focus semantics that make restriction interoperable.

evidence.detail: R4 root constraints include lastModified/authoredOn but not tsk-1.
R6 adds an error invariant restricting Task.restriction.
The old lastModified/authoredOn invariant is preserved with key tsk-0.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example has a restriction period but no fulfill code or focus. Under R6 `tsk-1`, it is invalid.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 turns a semantic expectation about `restriction` into an error invariant. This matters for migration because older data may have used restriction as a general scheduling or scoping field even when the Task was not explicitly a fulfillment of a request.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid Task with `restriction` and no matching fulfill code plus Reference focus can become R6-invalid. The invariant also rejects restriction with only `focus.valueCanonical`, even though canonical focus is otherwise allowed. Runtime validators and test fixtures need to distinguish the preserved `tsk-0` rule from new `tsk-1`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For every Task with `restriction`, verify that it is truly a fulfillment task. Add or correct `Task.code` and `focus.valueReference` only when that is semantically true. Otherwise move the data to `requestedPeriod`, input parameters, an extension, or a profile-specific field and review the business meaning.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning-first approach would have been easier for migration, but the error invariant provides stronger interoperability by preventing restrictions that cannot be interpreted consistently.

findings.title: R6 adds modifier element Task.doNotPerform to negate the Task

oldState.summary: R4 had no doNotPerform element on Task.
oldState.narrativeMd: A prohibition-style Task had to be represented through task code, focus semantics, profiles, or extensions.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional boolean doNotPerform with isModifier=true and isSummary=true.

flags.isModifierReason: If true, this element negates the Task. For example, instead of a request to perform a task, it is a request _not_ to perform a task.

semanticText.definition: If true indicates that the Task is asking for the specified action to not occur.

newState.narrativeMd: When true, the Task is a request not to perform the specified action.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not invalidate old R4 instances moving forward, but it is a high-risk downgrade/runtime change. An R4 system has no native field for `doNotPerform`; if it ignores or strips the R6 modifier, it can invert the task meaning.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ignoring `doNotPerform=true` can turn a prohibition into an instruction to act, which is a high clinical/business safety risk.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of representing negated tasks as explicit modifier content is strong and safety-relevant. Because R4 instances simply omit this optional element, this finding is not an R4-to-R6 base-design break for existing data. The major compatibility issue is that R6-to-R4 conversion must not silently drop a modifier that reverses task meaning.
justification.inferredGoal: Represent prohibition tasks directly and mark them as modifier content.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because `doNotPerform` is additive optional R6 content and does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using only a task code, profile convention, or modifier extension would be a different R6 design with weaker discoverability, not a backwards-compatible alternative needed to preserve R4 instances. Downgrade strategies such as extensions are mitigations for R4 consumers and should not be counted as base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The relevant risk is R6-to-R4 downgrade safety, not a less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R6 adds doNotPerform as 0..1 boolean.
R6 marks doNotPerform as a modifier and explains that it negates the Task.
R4 has no corresponding element.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example is valid R6 content that a direct R4 Task cannot carry safely.

findings.narrativeMd: `Task.doNotPerform` is an R6-only modifier. It is not just another optional element: `true` reverses the practical instruction conveyed by the Task.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is not broken by the addition because old instances simply omit it. R6-to-R4 is high risk: strict R4 validators reject the unknown element, while permissive or lossy adapters that drop it can create unsafe behavior. Generated R6 code must treat the element as modifier content.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Never silently drop `doNotPerform`. Downgrade only if a receiving R4 profile defines a modifier extension or other explicit prohibition representation. Add safety tests where `doNotPerform=true` and verify that legacy adapters reject or preserve the modifier semantics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A modifier extension would have been less disruptive to the base model but less reliable. Because negation is semantically critical, a base modifier is defensible despite cross-version risk.

findings.title: Task.input.value[x] and output.value[x] removed Contributor and added R6-only datatypes

oldState.summary: R4 input/output value[x] allowed many datatypes including Contributor.
oldState.narrativeMd: `valueContributor` was one of the valid R4 choice representations for Task input and output values.

newState.summary: R6 removes Contributor and adds integer64, CodeableReference, RatioRange, Availability, ExtendedContactDetail, and VirtualServiceDetail.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 expands the value choice for newer datatypes but no longer includes Contributor.

facts.note: Removed from both input.value[x] and output.value[x].

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 Tasks using `valueContributor` in input or output become invalid in R6 because the choice type is no longer allowed. R6 Tasks using the added datatypes cannot be represented by R4 Task without extensions or datatype-specific transforms.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning Task input/output choice types with the R6 datatype set is a reasonable goal. The less-breaking alternative depends on keeping `Contributor` available, at least as a legacy datatype choice, which is broader than a simple Task-local tweak and carries material maintenance cost. Because `valueContributor` use is likely rare and the datatype was removed from R6 core, the Task-local break is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Align Task input/output payload choices with the R6 datatype set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain Contributor as a deprecated Task input/output value choice, likely requiring broader R6 datatype support.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design would keep `Contributor` in the R6 datatype universe or allow it as a deprecated Task value choice so existing `valueContributor` instances remain valid. That is only a partial alternative for this Task finding because it pushes against global datatype evolution and would require validators, serializers, and generated models to keep supporting an otherwise removed datatype.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve rare `valueContributor` payloads but conflicts with R6 datatype cleanup and adds legacy support burden.

evidence.detail: R4 input.value[x] includes Contributor.
R4 output.value[x] includes Contributor.
R6 input.value[x] omits Contributor and adds R6 datatypes.
evidence.quote: integer64, CodeableReference, RatioRange, Availability, ExtendedContactDetail, VirtualServiceDetail

evidence.detail: R6 output.value[x] has the same type-domain change.

examples.examplesMd: The old example shows the choice name that is no longer allowed. The R6 example uses `valueCodeableReference`, which has no R4 input/output choice type.

findings.narrativeMd: Task input/output values are intentionally broad, so a choice-type list change is easy to overlook. The removed `Contributor` choice creates a hard break for old instances using `valueContributor`; the new R6 choices create downgrade gaps.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: `valueContributor` is old-valid/new-invalid. R6 choices such as `valueInteger64`, `valueCodeableReference`, `valueRatioRange`, `valueAvailability`, `valueExtendedContactDetail`, and `valueVirtualServiceDetail` are not R4-representable as native Task value choices. Generated models and serializers must update their choice unions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Search for `valueContributor` in Task input/output. Decide whether to map to an extension, a text/coding representation, ContactDetail/ExtendedContactDetail with loss, or reject. For R6-to-R4, use explicit extension policies for added datatypes and test every choice name in serialization.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The least disruptive alternative would be retaining Contributor as deprecated. Because Contributor is absent from R6 core, that would create a legacy exception in Task and require additional datatype support.

findings.title: Task terminology changed: status adds unknown and code binding strengthens to extensible

oldState.summary: R4 status used required ValueSet task-status|4.0.1 without unknown; Task.code had example binding to task-code.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required status codes came from the task-status code system; `Task.code` did not impose extensible conformance.

newState.summary: R6 status required binding adds unknown; Task.code binding is extensible and task-code adds instantiate and data-request.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 preserves existing R4 status codes but adds `unknown`; R6 also makes task-code the extensible baseline for Task.code.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Code lists were compared from local CodeSystem/ValueSet files. No live terminology expansion service was used.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 status codes remain valid in R6, so this is not an R4-to-R6 hard break for `status`. However, R6 `status=unknown` is not R4-representable, and arbitrary local Task.code codings may receive stronger conformance scrutiny under an extensible binding.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding `unknown` to status is not an R4-to-R6 break, but strengthening `Task.code` from example to extensible can affect conformance expectations for local action codes. Keeping example strength would be less disruptive, yet it would not meet the R6 goal of nudging common task actions toward standard codes as effectively. The binding change is therefore probably justified with a partial less-breaking alternative.
justification.inferredGoal: Improve interoperable task action/status vocabulary while preserving most existing status codes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Task.code` at example strength and publish standard task-code guidance or warnings.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would leave `Task.code` as an example binding while adding the new task-code concepts and narrative or best-practice guidance. This preserves maximum local-code freedom. The tradeoff is weaker semantic interoperability: validators could not expect standard codes when they apply, and cross-system task routing would remain more dependent on local conventions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would avoid stricter expectations for local codes but only partially achieves interoperable action coding.

evidence.detail: R6 task-status includes all observed R4 codes plus `unknown`.
R4 Task.code binding strength is example.
R6 Task.code binding strength is extensible.
R6 task-code adds `instantiate` and `data-request` compared with the observed R4 code system.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 status example is valid in R6 but not in R4 required task-status. The local Task.code example may still be acceptable under extensible binding if no standard code applies, but validators may require justification or issue warnings.

findings.narrativeMd: The required `Task.status` binding is mostly backward-compatible but adds an R6-only `unknown` status. The more behaviorally important R4-to-R6 conformance shift is `Task.code`: what was only an example binding is now extensible, so standard task action codes should be used when they fit.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 status values observed in the local code system remain valid in R6. R6 `status=unknown` is invalid against R4 required status. For `Task.code`, an R4 instance with a local code is not automatically invalid in R6, but extensible binding can produce validation warnings or failures under stricter profiles when a standard code is applicable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map common local task action codes to R6 task-code where possible, especially `instantiate`, `fulfill`, and `data-request`. Preserve local codings as additional codings when needed. Downgrade `status=unknown` using a profile-approved extension or reject if R4 consumers require the R4 code set.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The status code addition is additive for R6 but not downgrade-compatible. The Task.code binding could have stayed example strength; strengthening is likely intended to improve semantic interoperability for standardized task actions.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No external terminology expansion was performed; conclusions are based on local ValueSet compose and CodeSystem concept lists.

findings.title: R6 adds requester Group and restriction.recipient Device reference targets

oldState.summary: R4 requester did not allow Group; restriction.recipient did not allow Device.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 requester targets were Device, Organization, Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and RelatedPerson. R4 restriction.recipient targets were Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson, Group, and Organization.

newState.summary: R6 requester adds Group; restriction.recipient adds Device.

semanticText.comment: R6 comments limit Group requester use to family/household circumstances rather than practitioner groups.

newState.narrativeMd: These are target-domain widenings for R6, not R4-to-R6 validation breaks.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 instances are not invalidated because these are additions. New R6 instances using these targets cannot be represented as valid R4 Task requester or restriction.recipient references.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added Group requester and Device restriction-recipient targets support plausible R6 scenarios and do not invalidate existing R4 Tasks. Because this is target widening for R4-to-R6, there is no less-breaking base R6 design needed to preserve R4 instances. R4 downgrade handling remains important but is a conversion policy issue.
justification.inferredGoal: Allow Group requesters and Device restriction recipients in defined R6 scenarios.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because these are R6 reference target widenings that preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping the R4 target lists and using extensions for the new targets would reduce downgrade gaps, but that is not a backwards-compatible alternative for existing R4 data because no R4 instance is broken by these additions. It would also make the new R6 requester and recipient scenarios less visible to standard validation and search.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is an R6-to-R4 downgrade gap, not avoidable R4-to-R6 breakage.

evidence.detail: R4 requester target list does not include Group.
R6 requester target list includes Group.
R4 restriction.recipient target list does not include Device.
R6 restriction.recipient target list includes Device.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example uses both added target profiles and is not valid as a direct R4 Task.

findings.narrativeMd: These reference target additions are not breaking for existing R4 data, but they matter for bidirectional conversions and R4 clients consuming R6 Tasks.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is safe for these two paths. R6-to-R4 validation fails when requester is Group or restriction.recipient is Device. Semantically, requester Group also has an R6 narrative caveat: it is intended for family/household groups, not generic practitioner groups.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For downgrade, either reject these targets, map through extensions, or apply local business rules. Do not coerce Group requester to Organization or RelatedPerson unless a profile guarantees equivalence.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping the R4 target lists and using extensions would avoid downgrade gaps but make R6-supported scenarios less interoperable.

findings.title: Task.description type changed from string to markdown

oldState.narrativeMd: The field was plain free text in the model.

newState.narrativeMd: On the wire this is still a JSON string-like primitive, but the datatype and rendering expectation changed.

facts.note: No direct JSON shape break was identified.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard instance break for ordinary JSON payloads because markdown is serialized as a string and is a specialization of string. The risk is generated type changes and downstream renderers interpreting Markdown syntax in formerly plain text.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of advertising Markdown-capable human-readable descriptions to tooling is reasonable, and the change preserves ordinary R4 string instance compatibility on the wire. Since this is not a hard R4-to-R6 base-design break, the previous `Yes` alternative of leaving the datatype as string is better treated as a possible lower-churn design choice, not as an available backwards-compatible alternative needed to preserve R4 instances.
justification.inferredGoal: Allow optional Markdown presentation in task descriptions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because markdown keeps the primitive string wire shape and no R4 JSON description instance is rejected solely by this change.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have left `Task.description` typed as `string` and documented that Markdown may be used by convention, which would reduce codegen churn. However, because existing R4 primitive string values remain representable as markdown, the calibration category is `Not applicable`; implementers still need rendering and sanitization policy for Markdown-sensitive text.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The impact is mainly generated-type and rendering behavior, not old-valid/new-invalid base validation.

evidence.detail: R4 description type is string.
R6 description type is markdown.
R6 markdown primitive serializes through a string primitive value.

examples.examplesMd: The same JSON value is generally acceptable, but rendering can differ if the text contains Markdown metacharacters.

findings.narrativeMd: `Task.description` is wire-compatible for most JSON instances but not invisible to tooling. Generated models may expose a Markdown type, and UI renderers may process punctuation as Markdown formatting.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No ordinary R4 JSON string was identified that becomes invalid solely because of this Task-local type change. Runtime and codegen breaks are plausible for libraries that distinguish `string` and `markdown`, and UI behavior can change if descriptions are rendered as Markdown.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated models and rendering code. If existing descriptions must remain literal, escape or sanitize Markdown-sensitive characters before enabling Markdown rendering. Add tests for descriptions containing `*`, `_`, `#`, links, and raw HTML policies.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same goal could have been achieved by keeping `string` and documenting optional Markdown convention, but that would be less machine-readable for tooling.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R6 Task exists at the expected path with the same canonical URL, id, name, kind `resource`, type `Task`, abstract=false, and DomainResource baseDefinition. Maturity/status changes are noted as non-breaking governance changes.
No existing mandatory local element minimum was increased. Material max/representation changes are covered for `focus`, `statusReason`, `reason`, and related remodeled elements.

The lastModified/authoredOn invariant is semantically preserved as `tsk-0`; the material new `tsk-1` restriction invariant is reported as a finding. Inherited DomainResource constraint expression changes are out of scope.
No Task-local fixed values, pattern values, or default values were identified as added, removed, or changed.
No Task-local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were identified beyond datatype-level rules delegated to datatype reports.
No Task-local slicing changes were identified in the snapshot or differential.
The existing `Task.status` modifier flag remains true. The new modifier `Task.doNotPerform` is reported as a finding. Inherited `implicitRules`/`modifierExtension` behavior is out of scope.

No material removal of summary participation was identified for existing local business elements. New/changed summary participation follows reported element remodels such as `focus`, `doNotPerform`, and `performer`.

No resource-level serialization format change was identified. XML order and generated class impacts follow the reported element removals/additions/type replacements; JSON shape breaks are covered in the relevant findings.
Required status/code and extensible/example binding changes were checked against local terminology files. Full expansions, including external SNOMED performer-role, were not performed.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Task maturity/governance advanced to active normative/FMM 4
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical URL, resource type, kind, abstract flag, and baseDefinition remain stable. The standards-status/FMM/status change does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance impact is still important: implementers may treat R6 Task as more stable and may face stricter expectations for future changes than in R4 trial-use/FMM 2.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional Task.requestedPeriod
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element is optional and does not make existing R4 Tasks invalid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: It is an R6-to-R4 representability gap for stand-alone desired task timing. Downgrade requires an extension or local mapping, but the lower-risk addition did not warrant a separate high-impact finding.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Several example bindings gained explicit R6 value set URLs
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Example-strength bindings do not reject codes outside the value set. Adding `task-business-status` and `task-inputoutput-parameter-type` value set references is therefore guidance, not a hard validation break.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code systems and analytics may benefit from mapping local business/input/output labels to the new example code systems where appropriate.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Required intent and priority bindings changed version labels but observed code lists stayed stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The local package ValueSet/CodeSystem comparison found the same task-intent/request-intent and request-priority concepts used by the required bindings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validators will cite R6 value set versions, but no local code removal was identified for these two required elements.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Multiple Task-local remodels depend on CodeableReference (`statusReason`, `requestedPerformer`, `reason`, input/output values). A datatype-level report should own global CodeableReference behavior and conversion guidance.

Task structural moves (`focus`, `reason`, `performerType`/`requestedPerformer`, `performer`) likely affect search parameter expressions and client queries, but search parameters are outside this resource StructureDefinition report.

Inherited constraint and inherited element changes, such as the changed `dom-3` expression and inherited Resource/DomainResource element text, were intentionally excluded by the base-artifact scope rule.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: Contributor; integer64; RatioRange; Availability; ExtendedContactDetail; VirtualServiceDetail
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Task input/output value choice changes depend on datatype additions/removals. This report covers the Task-local allowed-type effect only; datatype-specific compatibility belongs to those datatype reports.

The performer-role binding includes SNOMED CT content. A terminology expansion would improve confidence for detailed code migration, but was not necessary to identify the structural performerType/requestedPerformer break.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Expected prevalence is based on element semantics and package definitions, not on a corpus of production R4 Task instances.
